component.name: Apache Traffic Server Ingress Controller
component.description: Kubernetes ingress integration on top of Apache Traffic Server. Its security model builds on the Traffic Server PMC's umbrella model (apache/trafficserver SECURITY.md), which remains canonical for the C++ core (proxy data plane, plugins, configuration loading), and adds two trust surfaces the umbrella model does not cover directly: the Kubernetes validating admission webhook and the translation of Ingress resources into Traffic Server remap.config / plugin.config routing directives.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.
Umbrella Traffic Server security model governing the C++ core surface.

blueprints.name: Ingress controller trust surfaces
blueprints.description: The two additional trust surfaces the ingress controller adds on top of the Traffic Server core: the validating admission webhook exposed to the Kubernetes API server, and the translation of resolved Ingress resources into Traffic Server routing configuration influenced by cluster users holding Ingress privileges.

assets.name: Validating admission webhook
assets.description: Webhook exposed to the Kubernetes API server. Requests originate from the control plane and are authenticated by the API server's TLS bearer-token bootstrap; the webhook bodies (proposed Ingress, Service, Endpoints, and ConfigMap payloads) are treated as adversary-controlled input on the wire.

assets.name: Ingress-to-remap.config translation
assets.description: Translates resolved Ingress resources into Traffic Server remap.config / plugin.config directives that route HTTP traffic to upstream Services; the routing table and therefore the proxy's outbound destinations are influenced by cluster users with Ingress create/update privileges.

zones.name: Kubernetes control plane
zones.description: The API server originating admission webhook requests, authenticated by TLS bearer-token bootstrap; the payloads it forwards are nonetheless adversary-controlled input.

zones.name: Cluster users with Ingress privileges
zones.description: Users holding Ingress create/update RBAC privileges in a namespace; the trust boundary is the RBAC scope on those resource kinds.

zones.name: Ingress controller and Traffic Server
zones.description: The controller process and the Traffic Server proxy whose routing it manages; the C++ core surface remains governed by the umbrella Traffic Server model.

threats.name: Malicious admission webhook payloads
threats.description: Webhook bodies (the proposed Ingress, Service, Endpoints, and ConfigMap payloads) are treated as adversary-controlled input on the wire; admission decisions and the parsing of those payloads must not crash, leak, or allow injection. Findings on admission-webhook handling are in scope for the ASF reporting process.

threats.name: Abuse of ingress-to-remap.config translation
threats.description: Cluster users with Ingress create/update privileges can influence the routing table and therefore the proxy's outbound destinations; the trust boundary is the RBAC scope on those resource kinds in the namespace. Defects in the translation of Ingress resources into remap.config / plugin.config directives that let a user exceed that RBAC scope are in scope for the ASF reporting process.

trustBoundaries.name: Admission webhook trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Requests are authenticated as coming from the API server, but the resource payloads they carry are adversary-controlled input on the wire.

trustBoundaries.name: Ingress RBAC trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The RBAC scope on Ingress (and related) resource kinds in the namespace bounds what a cluster user may legitimately make the proxy route; the translation code must not let influence exceed that scope.
